PREPARED IN RESPONSE TO TIFFANY'S OPERATIONS OVERVIEW

Tiffany's own description: "this is probably going to make you realize just how much of my business currently runs on Outlook reminders, sticky notes, coffee, and pure determination." That is exactly the right kind of honesty to start from. This document is the answer.

The Current State (Your Words, Mapped)

Tiffany's email lays out the operating reality clearly. The current stack works, but it is held together by Tiffany's personal memory and follow-through. Every hat is on her head except the physical labor. That works at one project per month. It does not scale to two.

What's working (keep)

ToolPurposeStatus
Pool Studio (Structure Studios)3D pool designKEEP. Industry standard for luxury custom builders. Integrates into the recommended stack.
QuickBooks OnlineAccounting, invoicing, drawsKEEP. Stays as the financial system of record. Recommended stack pushes data into QBO, not around it.
Outlook CalendarSchedulingKEEP, but reduce reliance. Outlook becomes a sync target, not the primary source of truth. Project pipeline tool takes over as the calendar driver.
Physical project foldersDocument storageREPLACE. Each project moves to a digital VDR (virtual data room). Physical folder for permits stays in the truck; everything else lives in the VDR.
Notes on phone and legal padsEverything elseREPLACE. Notes become CRM activities; legal pads become structured project records.

The Reference Architecture (Mark Has Built This Before)

The operational stack we are recommending for Cirilo is modeled directly on the backend Mark runs for markcmo.com: an admin dashboard, a customer CRM, an engagement pipeline, a customer portal, a document signing system, and a virtual data room. All of it custom-built, all of it interoperating, all of it owned by the business (not rented from a SaaS vendor at $399 per user per month).

Why this matters: a builder at your stage spends $400 to $1,500 per month per software seat across CRM, PM, signing, and portal SaaS. That stack is functional but never quite fits the actual workflow. The custom build pays for itself within 12 to 18 months, fits your 14-stage pool process exactly, and the data stays in your hands. No data export when you switch vendors. No per-project surcharges. No "this feature is in our Enterprise tier."

The Recommended System Stack

Eight components, each one mirroring a proven piece of the markcmo.com backend, adapted for the pool-build workflow.

01 · CORE
Admin Dashboard
Mirrors: markcmo.com /admin
Tiffany's command center. Single screen, every active pool project, every active lead, every open invoice, every scheduled milestone. Drag-drop kanban of the 14-stage pool build pipeline. Tap a project to drill in.
  • Pipeline view: all projects across 14 stages
  • Lead inbox: new inbound, awaiting follow-up
  • Today's calendar (consults, site visits, inspections)
  • This week's milestones at risk
  • Revenue dashboard: signed YTD, in-pipeline, projected
  • Reviews monitor (Google, Houzz, BBB) with one-click respond
02 · CORE
Customer CRM
Mirrors: mc_clients (markcmo backend)
Every lead, every prospect, every customer in one database. Contact info, project value, status, source attribution, all communication history. Linked to projects, invoices, and the customer portal.
  • Lead source tracking (Google, Houzz, referral, partnership)
  • Activity timeline: every call, email, SMS, meeting
  • Tags + segmentation (consultation booked, design pending, contract out)
  • Linked to Square customer ID for invoicing
  • Linked to QBO customer for accounting
  • Tiffany's notes per client (the legal-pad replacement)
03 · CORE
Project Pipeline (14 Stages)
Mirrors: mc_engagements + mc_documents
Custom-built around Tiffany's exact 14-stage pool construction sequence. Each pool project is one record. Each stage has its own milestone, owner, documents, photos, and inspection requirements.
  • Stages: Excavation, Rebar & Bonding, Long Plumbing, Electrical Rough-In, Gas, Inspections, Shotcrete/Gunite, Tile & Coping, Equipment, Decking, Interior Finish, Fill & Startup, Final Inspection, Closeout
  • Each stage: subcontractor assignment, target date, actual date, photos, inspection result
  • Permit tracking with submission and approval timestamps
  • Draw schedule auto-syncs to QBO invoicing
  • Subcontractor coordination panel (call/text/email from inside the project)
  • Outlook calendar sync (all milestones appear in Tiffany's calendar)
04 · CORE
Customer Portal
Mirrors: markcmo.com /portal/
Each pool client logs in to a branded Cirilo portal. Sees current stage, photo progress, plans, invoices, payment status, upcoming milestones. Reduces inbound "where are we?" calls by 60 to 80 percent.
  • Current stage and what comes next
  • Photo gallery (auto-updated as Tiffany uploads)
  • Document library (plans, permits, contracts, warranties)
  • Invoice and payment status
  • Direct message thread to Tiffany
  • Upcoming milestone calendar
  • Final orientation video + warranty page at closeout
05 · CORE
Document Signing
Mirrors: submit-engagement-doc pipeline
Custom e-signature flow for contracts, change orders, milestone acceptances, and warranty registrations. No DocuSign per-envelope fees. Audit log on every signature. Fully integrated with CRM and VDR.
  • Initial contract signing with deposit collection (Square)
  • Change order signing (homeowner approves, Tiffany countersigns)
  • Milestone acceptance signing (e.g., excavation done, homeowner confirms layout)
  • Final closeout + warranty registration signing
  • Every signed PDF stored in the project VDR
06 · CORE
Virtual Data Room (per Project)
Mirrors: markcmo.com /admin/vdr/
Replaces physical project folders. Every plan, permit, contract, photo, invoice, inspection report, and warranty doc for every project. Cirilo retains control; the homeowner sees a curated subset via the customer portal.
  • Pool Studio design exports (auto-deposited)
  • CAD plans and engineering docs
  • Permit applications and approvals
  • Subcontractor agreements
  • Invoices and draws (QBO synced)
  • Stage-by-stage photos
  • Inspection reports
  • Final closeout package
07 · AUTOMATION
Email + SMS Engine
Mirrors: Resend + Twilio integration
The "follow-up automation" Tiffany said was missing. Every lead, prospect, customer, and past client is in an appropriate cadence. Sub-1-minute response on inbound leads (conversion is 391 percent higher when contacted within 60 seconds).
  • Lead auto-response (web form, LSA call, Houzz message)
  • Consultation reminder (24h + 2h before)
  • Design phase nudges (decision-pending follow-up)
  • Proposal nudge sequence (3 / 7 / 14 day)
  • Construction milestone notifications (homeowner alerts)
  • Inspection scheduling automation
  • Project completion + review request automation
  • Long-term referral nudges (1-year anniversary, summer prep)
08 · AUTOMATION
Reporting & Dashboards
Mirrors: admin mc-dash-* widgets
What Tiffany needs to make decisions: pipeline health, source attribution, subcontractor scorecards, profitability per project, marketing ROI. All auto-calculated from the underlying CRM, pipeline, and QBO data.
  • Pipeline value (leads + active deals + signed)
  • Source attribution (which channels drive signed contracts)
  • Profit margin per project (real, not estimated)
  • Subcontractor performance (on-time delivery, defect rate)
  • Reviews velocity + star rating trend
  • Marketing spend ROI by channel
  • Time-from-lead-to-signed-contract
  • Weekly + monthly + quarterly auto-generated reports

Integration Map (How It All Connects)

The recommended stack is not eight isolated tools. It is one operational core with eight surfaces. Data flows in one direction wherever possible. Pool Studio designs flow to the VDR. QBO invoices flow to and from the project pipeline. The customer portal reads from the same source of truth Tiffany uses in the admin dashboard.

Build vs. Buy (What's Custom, What's SaaS)

FunctionRecommendationWhy
CRMCustom buildHubSpot Pro is $1,170/mo at 5 seats. Custom CRM owns your data, costs near-zero per month at scale, fits Cirilo's actual workflow. Same code pattern proven on markcmo.com.
Project Pipeline (14 stages)Custom buildBuildertrend is $399/mo and uses a generic 4-phase model. Your 14-stage sequence does not map to it. Custom = exact fit + lower TCO at 18 months.
Customer PortalCustom buildYour brand, your design language (rose gold and Cormorant), no Buildertrend or CoConstruct logo on the homeowner experience. Owns the relationship.
Document SigningCustom buildDocuSign is $25/envelope at the Enterprise tier. Two pools a month with 8+ signed docs per project = $400/mo and growing. Custom = zero per-envelope cost, already-proven pattern.
Virtual Data RoomCustom buildShareFile or Box charges per user and per GB. Custom = unlimited users (homeowner + subs + Tiffany), unlimited storage.
Email + SMS automationCustom build (Resend + Twilio)HubSpot is great until you hit the contact tier ceiling. Resend ($20/mo) + Twilio (pay per message) = pennies per active client.
Pool designBUY (keep Pool Studio)Industry standard. No reason to rebuild. Integrates via design export to VDR.
AccountingBUY (keep QuickBooks Online)Stays as the system of record for financials. Project pipeline pushes invoices to QBO via API.
Calendar bookingBUY (Calendly initially)$12/mo, mature product, works immediately. Migrate to custom inside customer portal in Phase 3.
Phone trackingBUY (CallRail)$45/mo. Industry standard. Attribution layer that ties phone leads back to source channels.
SMS sendingBUY (Twilio)Pay-per-message. Wired into the custom Email + SMS Engine.
Email sendingBUY (Resend)$20/mo + per-message. Powers the Email + SMS Engine. Same provider used on markcmo.com.
THE BUILD-VS-BUY HEURISTIC

Build custom anything that touches the homeowner experience or your core workflow. The customer portal, the project pipeline, the CRM, the signing flow, the VDR. These are differentiators. You should own them.

Buy SaaS for commodity infrastructure. Email delivery (Resend), SMS delivery (Twilio), phone tracking (CallRail), calendar booking (Calendly), accounting (QBO), and design (Pool Studio). These are utilities. Pay the fee and move on.

Phased Rollout (Aligned to the Marketing Roadmap)

The systems build deploys in parallel with the marketing roadmap. By Day 90, the trust scaffolding (marketing) and the operational core (systems) are both live. By Day 180, automation is running. By Day 365, the business operates as a system, not as Tiffany.

DAYS 1 TO 30 · FOUNDATION
Core CRM and Lead Capture
  • Custom CRM database stood up (mc_clients pattern for Cirilo)
  • Existing client list migrated from QBO into CRM
  • Lead capture form on cirilodb.com pushes to CRM
  • Auto-response email and SMS to new inbound leads (sub-1-minute)
  • Calendly published for design consult booking
  • Pool Studio design auto-export to VDR per project
Outcome: Every lead from Day 1 lands in a tracked system. Tiffany never loses a contact again.
DAYS 31 TO 60 · PIPELINE
14-Stage Project Pipeline + Subcontractor Coordination
  • Custom 14-stage pipeline tool deployed (matches Tiffany's construction sequence)
  • Active projects backfilled into the pipeline
  • Subcontractor coordination panel (one-click call, text, or email from inside a project)
  • Permit tracking with submission and approval timestamps
  • Outlook calendar two-way sync for all milestones
  • Stage-by-stage photo upload (mobile-friendly)
Outcome: Physical project folders retired. Every active pool has a digital pipeline record. Tiffany's calendar fills itself from project milestones.
DAYS 61 TO 90 · PORTAL + SIGNING
Customer Portal and Document Signing
  • Customer portal launched (Cirilo-branded, mobile responsive)
  • Each existing client gets login credentials
  • Document signing pipeline live (contracts, change orders, milestone acceptances)
  • VDR populated with all current project documents
  • Square deposit collection wired into contract signing
  • QBO invoicing tied to project draws (auto-create on milestone)
Outcome: Homeowners self-serve project status. "Where are we?" calls drop 60 to 80 percent. Contracts and deposits sign and clear in one online flow.
DAYS 91 TO 180 · AUTOMATION
Email + SMS Engine and Nurture Sequences
  • Lead nurture sequences live (cold, warm, hot)
  • Design-phase decision-pending nudges live (the "I'll think about it" rescue sequence)
  • Construction milestone auto-notifications to homeowner (excavation done, shotcrete in, etc.)
  • Inspection scheduling automation
  • Review request automation post-completion (auto-send 7 days after fill)
  • 1-year anniversary referral nudge
Outcome: Warm leads stop going cold. Reviews compound. Past clients become referral sources without Tiffany remembering to ask.
DAYS 181 TO 365 · OPTIMIZATION
Reporting Dashboards and Decision Layer
  • Source attribution dashboard (which channels drive signed contracts)
  • Profit margin per project tracking (real, not estimated)
  • Subcontractor performance scorecards (on-time delivery, defect rate)
  • Marketing spend ROI by channel
  • Time-from-lead-to-signed-contract by source
  • Weekly + monthly + quarterly auto-reports to Tiffany's inbox
Outcome: Tiffany makes decisions from data, not from gut. The first hires (PM, designer, foreman) are scoped against real numbers, not best guesses.

How This Fits With the Marketing Engagement

The systems build and the marketing engagement are two halves of the same plan. The marketing engagement (covered in the 12-Month Roadmap and the Partnership & PR Playbook) generates the leads. The systems build catches them, converts them, manages them through 14 stages of construction, and turns them into reviews and referrals at closeout.

The marketing engagement without the systems build = leaky bucket. Leads come in, get lost in Outlook, no one follows up, the ad spend wastes itself.

The systems build without the marketing engagement = beautifully organized empty pipeline. The system works, but there is nothing in it to manage.

Both are scoped in the pricing proposals (Models A, B, and C). On the discovery call we will match the tier and pricing model to Tiffany's cash position, growth goal (two pools per month), and risk tolerance.
